How should I choose a cloud percentage?

Use the share of model calls that policy and capability allow in Azure. Start from data requirements, not just the cheaper model. The percentage assumes the same token mix on each route.

A hybrid system keeps both environments available, so reducing Azure calls does not automatically reduce fixed search, hosting or network charges. Disable or resize those services explicitly. Learn how workload becomes usage →

Routing changes model token charges. Included provisioned infrastructure keeps billing even with no requests. Service quantities below are separate, explicit assumptions.

How do I estimate tokens and model calls?

Run a small set of real, representative tasks. Record total input, output and model calls, then divide by the number of calls or tasks. Include system instructions, conversation history, retrieved passages and tool messages.

If one task takes a planning call, a tool-review call and an answer call, enter three model calls per task. Billed reasoning is already part of output. For different task types, create separate saved scenarios. Walk through the $33 token example →

Why are there so many different units?

Azure charges different resources in different ways. App Service and AI Search use provisioned time. Logs and transfer use GB. OCR uses pages. Blob operations use groups of 10,000. The engine converts each quantity into its own billing unit before multiplying by price.

Expand a component to see its input quantities, source meter, rate and exact calculation. Change its frequency to one-time for initial processing where appropriate. Add omitted services explicitly. One Search replica is an example, not an availability guarantee.

Free grants default to zero available allocation. Enter only the allowance remaining for this solution at the subscription or billing-account scope. The engine prevents allocating a shared grant twice beyond its limit.

What changes when I already own the hardware?

Uncheck “Purchase this hardware now” to exclude a new purchase from upfront cash. Keep an allocated asset value so the monthly ownership comparison still includes amortization and maintenance.

Power uses average measured watts and powered hours, not just active working days. The PUE multiplier adds cooling and facility power. A $4,000 asset over 36 months allocates $111.11 per month; that amount is not added to the cash budget again.

Hardware value should include the GPU/CPU server, storage, network equipment and spares allocated to this solution. No residual value or hardware replacement is assumed. Monthly amortization is a planning allocation, not tax accounting.

05

Operations, licences and setup

People, local services and one-time implementation.

Which business costs should I include?

Count operations, support, local software, licences, backups, connectivity and the staff time allocated to this solution. Use one-time lines for setup, migration and rollout. Select the currency printed on your quote; the engine converts it consistently.

Leave a required price blank while you obtain a quote. The calculator will show a partial estimate instead of silently treating that cost as zero. Avoid entering maintenance or support both here and in the hardware percentage.

Add any services your design needs: identity licences, WAF/firewall/NAT/DNS, Content Safety, databases, backups, security plans, support, additional model groups or local software. An enabled line with usage and no price makes the estimate incomplete.

FOLLOW THE NUMBERS

How the whole-solution costing works.

Every total comes from the current workload, active components and stated price assumptions.

Edit solution inputs →
1

Calculate activity and route it

Users × tasks per day × days gives monthly tasks. Multiply by model calls per task, then apply the cloud percentage. Local calls consume local capacity without a cloud token charge.

—
2

Price the Azure token categories

Cloud input is split into ordinary, cache reads and separately priced writes. Each category and output is tokens ÷ 1,000,000 × its rate. Reasoning is included once in output.

—
3

Price each service in its billing unit

Usage after an allocated free grant ÷ billing-unit size × price. Time-based capacity uses provisioned hours; daily registry meters use days. Volume bands are calculated progressively.

—
4

Add local running costs

Power = devices × watts ÷ 1,000 × hours × PUE × electricity price. Maintenance = asset value × annual percentage ÷ 12. Add licences, support and operational labour.

—
5

Keep cash and amortization distinct

Monthly operating cash sums recurring costs. Monthly allocated cost adds asset value ÷ useful life. Upfront cash includes new hardware once plus one-time service lines; existing hardware adds no new purchase.

—
6

Build the planning budget

Reserve applies to monthly operating cash. Year 1 cash = upfront + 12 × monthly budget. The horizon uses the chosen number of months. Depreciation is not added to cash again.

—

What makes the estimate complete?

Every enabled component with billable usage needs a rate. Missing rates are shown as unpriced, and final totals are withheld. A zero rate is an explicit assumption, never a substitute for a missing price.

Completeness means the selected lines are priced. It does not prove that every required architectural service has been included.

EVERY NUMBER EXPLAINED

The model calculation, step by step.

This section explains the Model costs tab before applying the solution’s cloud-routing share. All rates are per 1,000,000 tokens.

1

Turn activity into model calls

Monthly tasks = users × tasks per user per day × active days. Model calls = tasks × average calls per task.

2

Calculate total input and output

Multiply model calls by average tokens per call. Include instructions, history, retrieved text and tools in input; include billed reasoning in output.

3

Split input into billing categories

Cache reads and separately priced writes are subsets of total input. Subtract them once to get ordinary input.

4

Apply the price to each category

Category cost = tokens ÷ 1,000,000 × rate. Add ordinary input, cache reads, cache writes and output.

5

Add services and a planning reserve

Base cost = model cost + other charges. Add the chosen allowance to the entire base. This reserve is your assumption, not an Azure charge.

6

Project the year and unit costs

Annual budget = monthly budget × 12, assuming unchanged rates and use. Per-task and per-user figures use model token costs only.

Itemized token calculation

USD
Tokens divided by one million multiplied by price per million
Billing categoryMonthly tokensPrice / 1MCalculationMonthly cost
Model token cost—

The calculator keeps full precision until display. Displayed rounding can create tiny differences when you add the visible line items. Read Azure's caching guidance ↗ and reasoning-token guidance ↗.

How do I compare this estimate with actual Azure charges?+

Run representative requests and record the API's usage fields. Divide measured token totals by model calls to replace the averages above. Use the same model, version, deployment, currency and reporting period.

Token categoryChat CompletionsResponses API
Total inputusage.prompt_tokensusage.input_tokens
Cache readsusage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokensusage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens
Output, including reasoningusage.completion_tokensusage.output_tokens

For supported newer Azure OpenAI models, the caching documentation also reports usage.prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens. Use provider-specific usage fields for other model families. Reasoning counts are already included in billed output; do not add them again.

In Azure Monitor, sum InputTokens, OutputTokens and TotalTokens over the same deployment and dates. In Azure Cost Management, select the correct resource or resource-group scope and group by Meter. Cost Management meter records and invoices establish actual billed cost; a price snapshot and forecast do not. Monitoring guide ↗ · Cost Management guide ↗

How do short-context and long-context prices work?+

Some models have separate tariffs based on the input length of each request. Select the tier that matches the threshold documented for your model. Monthly token totals and input-plus-output totals do not determine the tier.

If your workload mixes short and long requests, calculate those groups separately and add the costs. An average can hide requests that cross a pricing threshold. The calculator exposes explicit tier choices; it does not guess a threshold from a model's maximum context window. Azure model and context guidance ↗

What else affects my final bill?+

The Model costs tab covers text token costs using the selected Global PAYG rate schedule. PTU capacity, batch, priority processing, fine-tuning, managed compute, image, audio and video pricing use other rules. The Solution cost engine adds hosting, search, storage, embeddings, document processing, networking, monitoring, local equipment and operational costs. Add custom lines for any remaining services.

Taxes and negotiated discounts are not applied automatically. The Solution cost engine converts prices using its displayed FX snapshot or your override. Published model presets stay in USD; the model worksheet’s custom currency labels the rates you enter. Custom rates can represent your own agreement. Claude Consumption Unit billing is outside this token-rate calculator. Azure billing guidance ↗

Map the architecture to its cost.

Select a block to see what it does, how it is billed, and which calculator inputs to adjust.

Offline means locally complete

Pre-stage models, runtimes, dependencies, credentials, documents and local indexes. Cloud authentication, cloud search and Azure-hosted orchestration cannot be required in the disconnected request path.

Policy-restricted data stays local. If local capacity is unavailable, reject or queue the request rather than silently routing it to the cloud.

Model and embedding compatibility

Choose local models with the appropriate weights, licence and hardware support. A Foundry cloud model does not automatically have a downloadable local equivalent.

Use the same embedding model for indexing and querying each vector store. If the two environments use different embedding models, rebuild each index from approved source documents.

Azure vectorization guidance ↗

Choose the right local runtime

Foundry Local is designed for on-device applications. A shared inference server needs a runtime and capacity plan suited to concurrent users. Hardware sizing here is an assumption until benchmarked.

This diagram uses an independent local gateway. Azure API Management’s self-hosted gateway has its own tier and temporary-disconnection constraints.

LEARN AS YOU PLAN

A practical guide to AI costing.

Start with the basics, follow a worked example and learn what to measure before committing a budget.

Learn the numbers

From one question to a complete solution budget

Start with these six lessons, then change one assumption in the calculator and watch its effect. The goal is a forecast you can explain: workload, billable quantities, prices, infrastructure and a reserve for uncertainty.

Lesson 1

Understand what a token measures

A token is a piece of text processed by a model. It can be a word, part of a word or punctuation. Token counts vary with the model, language and content; a word count is only a rough starting point.

Input tokens include the question, instructions, conversation history, retrieved documents and tool results sent to the model. Output tokens cover generated content. A short question can therefore have a large input bill when your app attaches many documents.

Deep dive: reasoning and caching

Azure OpenAI reasoning models bill reasoning tokens as output, even when they do not appear in the visible answer. If reported output already includes reasoning, do not add it again. See Microsoft’s reasoning-token guide.

A cache read reuses eligible input computation at the selected model’s cache-read rate. Cache-write fees and eligibility vary by model. Use measured cache hits; repetition does not guarantee a hit. Classify each usage quantity according to its rate card so it is not counted twice. See Azure prompt caching.

Lesson 2

Count tasks, then count model calls

A task is what a person wants done, such as answering a support question. A model call is one request to a model. An agent might plan, search, review a tool result and draft an answer using several calls for one task.

Monthly calls = active users × tasks per user per day × active days × average model calls per task. Include billable retry attempts in the average model calls per task. Do not add retries again if your measured calls already include them.

Deep dive: replace guesses with measurements

Run representative tasks and record input, cached input, output, calls and successful outcomes. Include simple, typical and difficult examples. Calculate averages for each task type, then weight them by expected traffic. A support answer and a long document review should not automatically share one token average.

Use a typical scenario and a busy scenario. Check peak concurrency and latency separately: monthly token totals alone do not establish whether a deployment can keep up.

Lesson 3

Follow a complete token-cost example

This example uses the included GPT-5 mini USD snapshot: $0.25 per million input tokens and $2.00 per million output tokens. It assumes no cache savings, no retries and one model call per task. Check the model tab’s date and deployment details before reusing these rates; they are not your negotiated contract.

Example monthly workload and model cost
StepCalculationResult
Model calls100 users × 10 tasks × 22 days × 1 call22,000 calls
Input usage22,000 × 2,000 tokens44 million tokens
Input charge44 × $0.25$11.00
Output usage22,000 × 500 tokens11 million tokens
Output charge11 × $2.00$22.00
Model total$11.00 + $22.00$33.00
What changes if 80% of calls use Azure?

With the same token mix, Azure processes 17,600 calls. Its model charge becomes $33.00 × 80% = $26.40. The remaining 4,400 local calls still need hardware, electricity and operations. Add cloud and local infrastructure to obtain the solution total. A routing percentage does not automatically turn off either environment.

Source reference: Azure OpenAI pricing.

Lesson 4

Price every service in its own unit

The general rule is cost = billable quantity ÷ pricing unit × unit price. Keep the units aligned: 2 million tokens at a price per million means two pricing units. A price per 1,000 operations is different from a price per operation.

Examples of quantities to measure
ComponentQuantity
Generation and embeddingsTokens, with separate applicable rates
Compute and search capacityProvisioned instances or units × hours
Documents and storageProcessed pages, GB-month and operations
Logs and networkingIngested or transferred GB, plus applicable fixed charges
Deep dive: flat prices, tiers and free grants

A flat rate applies one price to the eligible quantity. Progressive pricing applies different prices to successive bands; do not apply the cheapest band to all usage. Subtract a confirmed free allowance only once, at its actual account, service and time-period scope. An allowance may already be used by another workload.

Read the meter’s region, deployment type and unit. Embedding documents during ingestion and embedding search questions are separate usage. Azure’s embedding guide explains this retrieval dependency.

Lesson 5

Separate running cost, purchase cost and budget

Operating cost pays for ongoing cloud services, electricity, support and staff time. Upfront cost pays for purchases and initial implementation. Local inference can avoid an API token charge while still carrying both kinds of cost.

A forecast is your best estimate. A budget may include a reserve: $1,000 forecast × 1.20 = $1,200 budget. That extra $200 is your 20% contingency, not an Azure service fee or a prediction that it will be spent.

Deep dive: amortization without double counting

For planning, a $12,000 server allocated across 36 months contributes about $333.33 per month, assuming no residual value. This allocation helps compare ownership with recurring cloud costs; it does not change when you pay the supplier.

Use monthly operating cost plus allocation for an economic comparison. Use hardware purchases plus implementation plus operating payments for a cash plan. Do not include the full purchase and its monthly allocation in the same total. App Service plan billing also illustrates why provisioned platform capacity remains a separate cost.

Lesson 6

Compare scenarios and choose a reporting currency

The sourced Azure rates use USD. A reporting currency converts the estimate for discussion: reporting amount = USD amount × reporting-currency units per USD. Record the exchange-rate date and source, or label a manually entered rate as an assumption.

Conversion does not select a different Azure region, retrieve a local Azure price list or reproduce your billing agreement. Follow the currency label on hardware and other manual inputs; an INR amount entered in a USD field changes the estimate incorrectly.

Deep dive: make a fair cloud/local comparison

Compare the same task volume, quality requirements and operating period. Keep fixed cloud and local services enabled when they are still required. Change one assumption at a time to understand its effect, then compare complete scenarios.

Results are financial estimates, not hardware sizing or capacity validation. Confirm model fit, measured throughput, availability and data-routing policy separately. Offline operation also needs local retrieval, identity and secrets; see Foundry Local’s deployment scope.

Plain-language glossary

Token
A small unit processed by a model.
Input tokens
Content sent into a model call.
Output tokens
Generated tokens counted by the provider.
Reasoning tokens
Internal generated work; check output billing.
Cache read
Reuse of eligible previously processed input.
Cache write
Creating reusable cached input; fees vary.
Task
One user goal or business activity.
Model call
One request to a model endpoint.
Retry
Another attempt after an unsuccessful request.
RAG
Retrieving information to supply to a model.
Embedding
A numeric representation used for similarity search.
Rate
The price for a defined billing unit.
Billing unit
The amount covered by one quoted price.
Free grant
An eligible allowance with limits and scope.
Fixed cost
Cost retained while provisioned capacity is kept.
Variable cost
Cost that changes with measured consumption.
Upfront cost
Purchase or setup cash paid initially.
Amortization
Allocating a purchase across a planning period.
Reserve
Extra budget for uncertain future spending.
Reporting FX
An exchange rate used to display the estimate.

Questions people usually ask

Why could my Azure invoice differ?

Actual usage, price dates, regional meters, negotiated terms, taxes, allowances and currency treatment may differ. Reconcile usage and meter identifiers before comparing totals.

Why does reducing cloud traffic not remove all cloud cost?

Provisioned compute, search and networking can remain enabled. Review those quantities separately from token consumption.

Is the lowest token price the best choice?

Compare cost per successful task. Extra calls, retries or longer answers can offset a cheaper token rate. Test quality with your own examples.

Does this budget stop my services at the limit?

No. This calculator estimates spending; it does not enforce a spending cap or change your Azure resources.

When should I update the estimate?

Before a purchasing decision and whenever traffic, model, deployment, rates or architecture changes. Replace assumptions with measured usage as it becomes available.

HOST THIS CALCULATOR ON AZURE

Deploy to Azure App Service.

A small Node server serves the calculator. Calculations and scenario files stay in the browser.

App Service edition · keep your original ZIP for redeployment.

What you are deploying

The downloaded ZIP hosts this calculator with a small Node server. It includes the page, pricing evidence, exchange rates, architecture and help. It does not create the AI models, Azure services or local inference platform shown in the architecture.

1. Download the ready-to-run package

Use the ZIP button above. It contains server.cjs, package.json, README-AZURE.md and dist/ directly at its root. No npm dependencies or build step are required. Keep the ZIP intact and upload it to Azure Cloud Shell if you use Cloud Shell.

The server listens on Azure’s process.env.PORT at 0.0.0.0, serves only dist/ and returns 404 for unknown routes. The complete guide is inside the ZIP. Microsoft ZIP deployment guide ↗

2. Sign in and confirm a supported Node runtime

Run these commands in Bash using a current Azure CLI. Select the subscription that will pay for hosting. The package targets Node 24 LTS; confirm it appears in the runtime list. If you choose another supported LTS, update the package’s engines.node field and rebuild the ZIP.

az login
az account set --subscription "YOUR-SUBSCRIPTION-ID"
az webapp list-runtimes --os-type linux --runtime node --support active --output table

Node configuration documentation ↗ · Current CLI reference ↗

3. Create a paid Linux App Service plan and app

Replace the app name with an available name. This example uses one Linux B1 instance. The verified East US 2 retail rate is $0.017 per instance-hour, or $12.41 for 730 hours, before any additional services or taxes. B1 is a starting assumption for this calculator; benchmark and size the full AI backend separately. Confirm availability and your agreement’s price before creating resources.

COSTING_RG="rg-foundry-calculator"
COSTING_REGION="eastus2"
COSTING_PLAN="asp-foundry-calculator"
COSTING_APP="YOUR-GLOBALLY-AVAILABLE-APP-NAME"
COSTING_RUNTIME="NODE:24-lts"
COSTING_ZIP="./foundry-cost-planner-app-service.zip"

az group create --name "$COSTING_RG" --location "$COSTING_REGION"

az appservice plan create   --resource-group "$COSTING_RG" --name "$COSTING_PLAN"   --location "$COSTING_REGION" --is-linux --sku B1

az webapp create   --resource-group "$COSTING_RG" --plan "$COSTING_PLAN"   --name "$COSTING_APP" --runtime "$COSTING_RUNTIME" --https-only true

The App Service plan is billed for its provisioned instances, even when one app is stopped. Apps sharing a plan share that compute charge. Plan billing and tiers ↗

4. Configure startup and deploy the ZIP

Keep remote build off because the bundle is ready to run. The startup command must be node server.cjs. After deployment, open https:// followed by the actual hostname returned by Azure.

az webapp config set   --resource-group "$COSTING_RG" --name "$COSTING_APP"   --startup-file "node server.cjs" --always-on true --min-tls-version 1.2

az webapp config appsettings set   --resource-group "$COSTING_RG" --name "$COSTING_APP"   --settings NODE_ENV=production SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=false   --output none

az webapp deploy   --resource-group "$COSTING_RG" --name "$COSTING_APP"   --src-path "$COSTING_ZIP" --type zip

az webapp show   --resource-group "$COSTING_RG" --name "$COSTING_APP"   --query defaultHostName --output tsv

5. Configure access for your audience

The private access settings of this ChatGPT Site do not transfer in the files. For an internal calculator, open App Service → Authentication → Add identity provider → Microsoft. Use your organization’s Entra tenant, require authentication and choose HTTP 302 redirect for browser sign-in. Configure the intended user or group assignments and test with both allowed and unauthorized accounts before sharing the URL.

The calculator needs no Azure API keys. If you later add an AI backend, use server-side managed identity and grant the required service permissions; do not place credentials in browser files.

Microsoft Entra authentication ↗ · Managed identity ↗

6. Verify and update

Check all six tabs, the model catalog, currency conversion, scenario controls, architecture links and CSV/JSON downloads. If the app fails to start, inspect its logs. Check the ZIP root, runtime, dist/index.html and startup command first.

az webapp log config   --resource-group "$COSTING_RG" --name "$COSTING_APP"   --docker-container-logging filesystem

az webapp log tail --resource-group "$COSTING_RG" --name "$COSTING_APP"

For an update, deploy a new package to the same app. Pricing and FX remain dated snapshots until the application data is refreshed. This package does not retrieve your Azure invoice.

Hosting the complete AI application

App Service can host the user interface and an orchestration API. Deploy Foundry models, AI Search, storage, embeddings, monitoring, secrets and networking as separate resources. The solution engine budgets these separately from the web host.

Review the component architecture →

Keeping the offline branch usable

A cloud-hosted app cannot deliver the offline path during a full internet outage. Deploy a local interface, gateway, identity, models, vector store, documents and operations. Synchronize approved data and packages when connectivity and policy allow.
